assessments.reasoning: The digest-matched OpenJDK publisher capture 4f3a8b6bb5e04b2c9fa4462e779170bc places “version 2 only” in the opening of the notice itself. The same passage states the module, executable-distribution and modification conditions.

SPDX capture 0a6f9fbd6a274cc0b28b024df81f05fa reproduces “version 2 only” in licenseExceptionText and retains the Oracle module conditions. The optional introduction in its matching template has no bearing on the words actually present in the publisher notice.

challenge.method: Tested GPL-2.0-or-later, GPLv3, a Classpath-based grant and an executable containing an arbitrary independently licensed module against the opening and the proviso.
challenge.results: “Only” resolves the base variant. The phrase “regardless of the license terms” qualifies modules already designated through Oracle's cited list. It supplies no basis for treating an arbitrary module as designated. The separate Classpath reference does not alter either boundary.

limitations: GPL-2.0-only identifies the base for the defined OpenJDK Code. Module versions, individual copyright-holder decisions and particular distributions were outside the inspected evidence.
The relationship reviewed is the named base edition. Resolution of the registry's opaque target ID was outside the supplied source set.
reasoning: The notice identifies the GNU General Public License and expressly says “version 2 only ("GPL2")”. Its permission allows linking the defined OpenJDK Code with Designated Exception Modules to produce an executable and copying and distributing that executable under GPL2, provided the modules continue under the licenses Oracle offered. For modified or added OpenJDK code, the text conditions combination on the copyright holder making the new GPL2 code subject to the exception.
